inspection_summary: Verified the frozen SHA-256 and 1047-line count, then inspected every normalized line. The source develops two rationally weighted arg-zeta contour families, exposes their off-critical-zero correction terms and sign conditions, derives modulus and zero-counting representations, relates Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor criteria, and reports finite-cutoff numerical checks. Formula extraction is fragmented but the prose is coherent enough to recover the mechanisms; exact displayed identities require scan verification before formula-level reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic framing and a high-level claim that the paper emphasizes argument-of-zeta integral criteria and subsumes earlier criteria.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recalls the rectangular-contour and generalized-Littlewood method and motivates changing from log-modulus to argument integrals.

sections_inspected.label: First weighted argument-integral family
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs a two-denominator rational kernel, computes pole and zero contributions, obtains a general identity, and specializes it to sign-definite RH-equivalent criteria including a pole-collision limit.

sections_inspected.label: Repeated-pole weighted argument-integral family
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a double-pole kernel to derive a second criterion family, its limiting form, an alternative differentiation derivation, and a tractability obstruction for transferring that derivation to the first kernel.

sections_inspected.label: Pole-cancelled real-axis and vertical-line relation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Replaces zeta by zeta times z minus one, uses a semi-indented contour, and produces a principal-value modulus identity with sign-definite off-line-zero corrections.

sections_inspected.label: Zero-sum interpretation and Volchkov analysis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the zero-counting function and Stieltjes integration to interpret argument integrals as zero sums, recover Volchkov, transform through an integrated argument function, and compare modulus criteria.

sections_inspected.label: Numerical results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports finite-truncation checks for three identities, parameter-dependent convergence, and a principal-value computation.

sections_inspected.label: Conclusion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the reusable kernel-selection plus generalized-Littlewood recipe and its practical aspiration.

sections_inspected.label: References, affiliations, and figures
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: References and metadata are non-unit-bearing; extracted figures give captions but not enough graphical content for independent mathematical use.

accepted_units.title: Rectangular contour weights turn log-zeta into argument integrals
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction isolates the reusable design move: choose a rational weight on a rectangular contour, discard remote sides, and use parity to target the imaginary rather than real part of log-zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact branch convention is supplied in lines 114-116 inside the first construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on complex-log branch choice, contour orientation, decay on remote edges, and OCR-fragmented displayed kernels.

accepted_units.unit_type: contour setup for weighted arg-zeta integrals
accepted_units.title: Two-scale odd kernel and its pole/zero accounting
accepted_units.why_material: This carried v1 span constructs the first rational kernel, uses parity to isolate arg-zeta, fixes the argument convention, and explains how kernel poles, the zeta pole, and nontrivial zeros enter the contour value.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed equality announced at the end continues through line 196; that completion is recorded as a v1 context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the continuous-path convention for arg-zeta and on formula layout whose fractions are split across text lines.

accepted_units.title: General first-family identity separates baseline terms from off-line zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The general identity makes the diagnostic structure explicit: a closed-form baseline is corrected by a sum over zeros to the right of b, after which a change of variables gives a sufficient kernel-parameter range making every such correction share a sign.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 226-230 invoke an externally reported finite zero verification only to justify the numerical parameter cap used in the theorem; the source itself does not establish that verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The sign claim depends on the algebra of the displayed rational expression and on a bound for the lowest possible off-line zero ordinate; exact constants need formula and provenance checking.

accepted_units.title: First-family equality and its pole-collision specialization detect zeros right of b
accepted_units.why_material: This carried v1 span states the iff criterion, identifies b equals one half as RH-equivalent, and shows that a seemingly singular parameter choice has a finite Laurent-limit producing a second criterion of the same family.
accepted_units.context_note: The iff direction relies on the sign analysis in lines 197-232, which is therefore recorded as required surrounding context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on exact rational weights, limiting treatment at the pole of zeta, and the stated finite parameter bound; displayed equations are OCR-fragmented.

accepted_units.title: A double-pole kernel yields a derivative-of-zeta criterion family
accepted_units.why_material: Changing the kernel to a squared denominator changes the residue into a logarithmic derivative of zeta while retaining an explicit off-line-zero sum whose paired contributions can be made sign-definite.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the derivational setup needed to interpret the carried theorem statements beginning at line 416.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a second-order residue calculation, conjugate-zero pairing, and accurate recovery of several densely fragmented formulas.

accepted_units.title: Double-pole argument criterion and its Laurent-limit form
accepted_units.why_material: This carried v1 span states the second iff criterion, its RH specialization, and a limit at a plus b equals one whose constant involves Euler's constant, then begins an independent derivation by integration by parts.
accepted_units.context_note: The contour derivation lies in lines 331-415 and the alternative derivation completes in lines 501-541; both are captured by one context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the chosen arg-zeta branch, the double-pole kernel, the Laurent expansion at one, and OCR-sensitive displayed constants.

accepted_units.title: Integration by parts links argument criteria to differentiated modulus identities
accepted_units.why_material: The source derives the same second-family equality by integrating the complex argument integral by parts and differentiating an earlier log-modulus identity with respect to b, showing two representations of the same zero correction.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivation assumes RH temporarily to obtain the clean identity and then restores the general zero terms by differentiating their contribution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on boundary-term decay, parameter differentiation under the integral, and an earlier identity quoted in the source; exact formulas need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: The modulus-differentiation route does not transfer cleanly to the two-scale kernel
accepted_units.why_material: A partial-fraction antiderivative would require a log-modulus integral with an extra logarithmic kernel, for which the authors identify no tractable route, motivating direct contour analysis instead.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a bounded negative result about method transfer, not a proof that no alternative treatment exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the displayed antiderivative and on the authors' tractability assessment.

accepted_units.title: Cancelling the zeta pole converts a vertical argument setup into a modulus identity
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing zeta by zeta times z minus one removes the simple pole from the logarithm, and a semi-indented contour relates a vertical critical-line modulus integral to a real-axis principal-value integral.
accepted_units.context_note: The equality is defined with an explicit Cauchy principal value around x equals one and is proposed as numerically suitable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the pole-cancelling factor, the geometry of a figure-defined semi-contour, Laurent behavior at one, and OCR-sensitive integral limits.

accepted_units.title: Off-critical zeros perturb the pole-cancelled modulus identity with one sign
accepted_units.why_material: The source computes the imaginary contribution of a zero right of the critical line and observes that all positive-ordinate contributions have one sign, turning the modulus identity into an RH-equivalent criterion and suggesting analogous semi-contour relations.
accepted_units.context_note: The claimed extension to other weights is only sketched and no additional formulas are developed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The equivalence depends on the explicit zero-contribution formula, conjugation/multiplicity conventions, and the semi-contour setup in the preceding unit.

accepted_units.title: Stieltjes integration maps arg-zeta weights to sums over zero ordinates
accepted_units.why_material: The zero-counting formula identifies arg-zeta as the fluctuating term in N(x); choosing a weight G and integrating against dN converts a sum over zero ordinates into a weighted argument integral and recovers Volchkov's RH criterion as the b equals one-half case of Theorem 2a.
accepted_units.context_note: The sum comparison uses a known closed form quoted by the source and presumes the relevant Stieltjes integrals and boundary terms exist.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the normalization and branch of the zero-counting formula, Stieltjes integration by parts, and formula extraction of G and its derivative.

accepted_units.title: Integrated argument converts Volchkov's criterion into a two-dimensional log-modulus criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Introducing the integrated argument S1, applying integration by parts, and using a Littlewood relation expresses the argument criterion through horizontal integrals of log-modulus; the source notes this representation is harder to handle but generalizes it to its other equality.
accepted_units.context_note: The source treats the constant horizontal term as vanishing after differentiation and states equation 17 as RH-equivalent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the growth estimate for S1, a quoted Littlewood relation, interchange of integrations, and heavily fragmented nested-integral typography.

accepted_units.title: Resolvent-like zero sums generate a parameterized Volchkov family
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing the original reciprocal quadratic zero weight by a shifted resolvent sum yields another closed-form zero identity and, through the same N(x) integration, a family identified with Theorem 2 at b equals one half.
accepted_units.context_note: The text sketches rather than fully writes the resulting equality, so the mechanism is stronger evidence than the exact final formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a quoted partial-fraction identity for the logarithmic derivative of zeta and on matching the shift parameter to the kernel.

accepted_units.title: Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor are two representations of one contour criterion
accepted_units.why_material: By tracing the argument criterion back to a differentiated prior log-modulus theorem, the source argues that the Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor equalities are the same underlying criterion written in different integral representations.
accepted_units.context_note: The prior theorem is reproduced in the span, but its original proof is not part of this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the validity of the quoted earlier theorem and the representation transformations developed in lines 466-541 and 749-810.

accepted_units.title: Finite-cutoff tests compare convergence across criteria and parameters
accepted_units.why_material: The authors report matched small discrepancies for three argument-integral identities, examine improvement as b approaches the known zero-free border, and separately test the principal-value modulus identity, providing diagnostics of numerical behavior rather than proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The runs use Mathematica, finite integration cutoffs, listed zeros, and rounded results; no independent reproducibility details or error bounds beyond discrepancies are supplied.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on external zero tables, numerical singularity handling, finite truncation, and an absent graphical plot for the parameter sweep.

accepted_units.title: Kernel selection plus generalized Littlewood supplies a criterion-design template
accepted_units.why_material: The conclusion abstracts the paper's mechanism into selecting g, evaluating the log-zeta contour, and seeking an equality whose omitted zero contributions are diagnostic of RH.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a design heuristic and aspiration; the source does not establish that a practically decisive kernel exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on admissible decay, singularity control, branch conventions, and sign or identifiability of the resulting zero corrections.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Kernel geometry controls the zero-penalty diagnostic
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For both rational weight families, contour evaluation separates an explicit baseline from contributions of zeros right of b; kernel parameters are then restricted so those contributions cannot cancel, converting equality with the baseline into a zero-free-half-plane criterion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The usable parameter cap relies on a quoted finite zero verification and on OCR-sensitive sign algebra, so it is not independently certified by this source text.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Argument, modulus, and zero sums are linked representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Integration by parts, pole cancellation, the zero-counting function, and the integrated argument transform the same contour information among weighted arg-zeta integrals, log-modulus integrals, and sums over zeros, explaining the correspondence among named criteria.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Each transformation carries distinct convergence, principal-value, branch, or quoted-theorem assumptions; equivalence of representations does not make them equally tractable numerically or analytically.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Criterion construction is constrained by tractable kernels
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The general recipe of choosing a contour kernel is useful only when remote edges vanish, residues and zero corrections are computable, and the resulting correction is identifiable; the failed modulus transfer illustrates a concrete tractability boundary.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion offers a search heuristic, not evidence that some kernel from this class can prove or disprove RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite-cutoff convergence is a diagnostic, not equivalence evidence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The numerical section probes how several formally RH-equivalent representations behave under finite truncation and observes improved agreement near a known zero-free boundary, which can help compare numerical conditioning across kernels.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The calculations assume finite zero data and provide neither a proof nor sensitivity to a hypothetical high off-line zero.
